# QuasarDeconData

QuasarDeconData bundles processed peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) deconvolution benchmark datasets together with a combined 10x Genomics single-cell PBMC reference, all formatted for use with QUASAR deconvolution workflows.

The bulk benchmark datasets listed below and the healthy 10x PBMC reference use the same six cell-type labels in their harmonized annotations: `Bcells`, `CD4Tcells`, `CD8Tcells`, `Monocytes`, `NK`, and `Unknown`. Column order and gene identifier formats vary, so align them before benchmarking.

The COVID-19 references and pseudo-bulk datasets retain their own cell-type annotations.

## Installation

You can install the development version of QuasarDeconData from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("SergejRuff/QuasarDeconData")
```

## Datasets

| Object | Platform | Features | Samples / Cells | Ground truth | ID element |
|------------|---------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|

| `load_cov_imm("test")` | COVID-19 PBMC scRNA | genes in Seurat object | test cells | `cell_type` | `donor_id` |
| `load_cov_imm("healthy")` | COVID-19 PBMC scRNA (healthy donors only) | genes in Seurat object | healthy cells | `cell_type` | `donor_id` |
| `load_cov_pbulk()` | COVID-19 PBMC pseudo-bulk | matched expression features | 10 × 1000 samples | 1000 × 11 per file | — |
| `load_cov_pbulk("train")` | COVID-19 PBMC pseudo-bulk | matched expression features | 10,000 samples | 10,000 × 11 | — |
| `load_cov_pbulk("healthy")` | COVID-19 PBMC pseudo-bulk (healthy donors only) | matched expression features | healthy samples | matched proportions | — |
| `GSE107011` (Monaco1) | RNA-seq | 36,128 | 12 | 12 × 6 | `ensembl_ids` |
| `GSE107990` (Monaco2) | Microarray (Illumina HT-12 V4) | 20,908 | 164 | 164 × 6; additional 164 × 11 | — |
| `GSE107572` | RNA-seq | 19,423 | 9 | 9 × 6 | — |
| `GSE120502` | RNA-seq | 39,376 | 249 | 249 × 6 | `gene_ids` |
| `GSE65133` | Microarray (Illumina HT-12 V4) | 35,688 | 20 | 20 × 6 | `probe_ids` |
| `GSE193141` | RNA-seq (raw counts) | 39,376 | 156 | 156 × 6; additional 156 × 8 | — |
| `SDY67` | RNA-seq | 23,113 | 231 | 231 × 6 | — |
| `SDY67_scaden` | RNA-seq | 11,328 | 12 | 12 × 6 | — |



Note: `GSE107990` and `GSE65133` contain microarray intensity measurements rather than sequencing counts. 

## Single-cell reference

The reference is a processed Seurat object combining the 10x 6k, 8k, and 10k healthy-donor PBMC datasets. Cell-type labels live in `celltype` and the dataset of origin in `donor_id`.

```{r ref}
library(QuasarDeconData)

pbmc_sc_ref <- load_pbmc_sc_ref()
pbmc_sc_ref

# cell-type composition
table(pbmc_sc_ref$celltype)

# dataset of origin
table(pbmc_sc_ref$donor_id)
```

## Bulk benchmark datasets

Each bulk dataset is a named list containing:

- `bulk_expression_profiles`: expression values arranged as features × samples.
- `ground_truth_proportions`: reference proportions arranged as samples × cell types.

Some datasets also contain a separate gene or probe identifier vector. For `SDY67` and `GSE107990`, gene symbols are stored in the expression row names. For `GSE193141`, the expression row names contain NCBI gene identifiers.

Two datasets additionally contain `ground_truth_all_ct`: `GSE193141` retains eight original population measurements, and `GSE107990` retains eleven. 

```{r bulk-single}
data(GSE107011)

names(GSE107011)

dim(GSE107011$bulk_expression_profiles)
dim(GSE107011$ground_truth_proportions)

# Six-column reference proportions
head(GSE107011$ground_truth_proportions)
rowSums(GSE107011$ground_truth_proportions)
```

Load the remaining datasets and compare their dimensions:

```{r bulk-all}
data(GSE107990)
data(GSE107572)
data(GSE120502)
data(GSE65133)
data(SDY67)
data(GSE193141)
data(SDY67_scaden)
data(GSE107011)

bulk_datasets <- list(
  GSE107011    = GSE107011,
  GSE107990    = GSE107990,
  GSE107572    = GSE107572,
  GSE120502    = GSE120502,
  GSE65133     = GSE65133,
  SDY67        = SDY67,
  SDY67_scaden = SDY67_scaden,
  GSE193141    = GSE193141
)

t(vapply(
  bulk_datasets,
  function(x) {
    c(
      features = nrow(x$bulk_expression_profiles),
      samples = ncol(x$bulk_expression_profiles),
      cell_types = ncol(x$ground_truth_proportions)
    )
  },
  integer(3)
))
```

All listed bulk benchmarks expose the same cell-type labels in `ground_truth_proportions`, although their column order varies:

```{r celltypes}
lapply(
  bulk_datasets,
  function(x) colnames(x$ground_truth_proportions)
)
```

### SDY67

`SDY67` contains 23,113 genes and 231 samples with complete six-column proportions. RNA and flow cytometry measurements were matched by participant and collection visit.

The proportions combine measurements from the innate and Treg panels:

- `Monocytes` combines classical, intermediate, and non-classical monocytes.
- `CD4Tcells`, `Bcells`, and `NK` use their corresponding source gates.
- `CD8Tcells` uses the study-labeled CD8 gate, which is a CD4-low/negative T-cell proxy. CD8 was not directly measured by this panel.
- `Unknown` is calculated as one minus the sum of the five selected populations.

The combined proportions are an approximate composition. `Unknown` can include unassigned cells and differences between the panels' gates. Samples with missing or ambiguous panel matches, or overlapping main CD4/CD8-proxy gates, were excluded.

`SDY67_scaden` are the same 12 bulk samples along the corresponding ground truth proportion vectors used in the scaden paper and other works such the DISSECT paper.

```{r sdy67}
dim(SDY67$bulk_expression_profiles)
dim(SDY67$ground_truth_proportions)

# Expression columns and proportion rows have identical sample ordering
identical(
  colnames(SDY67$bulk_expression_profiles),
  rownames(SDY67$ground_truth_proportions)
)
```



## COVID-19 single-cell references

QuasarDeconData also includes a donor-balanced COVID-19 PBMC immune reference split into training and test sets. The split balances mild and severe COVID-19 donors so that neither half is enriched for disease severity.

The training split is intended as the single-cell reference for deconvolution methods, while the test split was used to generate the packaged COVID-19 pseudo-bulk benchmark datasets.

A third reference, `load_cov_imm("healthy")`, contains cells from non-diseased donors only. It exists for reference-mismatch experiments, where a reference that does not match the disease composition of the mixtures is deliberately used for deconvolution.

```{r covid-sc, eval=FALSE}
train_cov   <- load_cov_imm("train")
test_cov    <- load_cov_imm("test")
healthy_cov <- load_cov_imm("healthy")

train_cov
test_cov
healthy_cov

# cell-type composition
table(train_cov$cell_type)
table(test_cov$cell_type)
table(healthy_cov$cell_type)

# donor IDs retained for subject-aware methods such as MuSiC
table(train_cov$donor_id)
table(test_cov$donor_id)
table(healthy_cov$donor_id)
```

All three objects are returned as Seurat objects with cell-type identities set from `cell_type`. The `donor_id` metadata column is retained for deconvolution methods that require per-subject information.

Note that the healthy reference may lack cell types that are present in the pseudo-bulk ground truth. Methods cannot recover a cell type absent from the reference, so predicted proportion matrices from the healthy reference can have fewer columns than the corresponding `ground_truth_proportions`. Align the two explicitly — for example by padding the missing cell types with zeros — before computing benchmark metrics.

## COVID-19 pseudo-bulk benchmarks

The COVID-19 pseudo-bulk datasets were generated from `test_cov` and are intended for deconvolution benchmarking with `train_cov` as the reference. The package contains ten independent pseudo-bulk files, each with 1000 simulated bulk samples.

Pseudo-bulk data generated from the training split (10,000 samples) and from the healthy-only split are also available. Both are stored as chunks internally and reassembled on load, so the split is not visible to the caller.

Each pseudo-bulk object contains two elements:

- `bulk_expression_profiles`: pseudo-bulk expression profiles.
- `ground_truth_proportions`: true cell-type proportions for each pseudo-bulk sample.

```{r covid-pbulk, eval=FALSE}
# load all ten test pseudo-bulk datasets
cov_pbulks <- load_cov_pbulk()

length(cov_pbulks)
names(cov_pbulks)

# load one specific pseudo-bulk dataset
cov_pbulk_1 <- load_cov_pbulk(1)

names(cov_pbulk_1)

dim(cov_pbulk_1$bulk_expression_profiles)
dim(cov_pbulk_1$ground_truth_proportions)

# ground-truth proportions sum to 1 per sample
head(cov_pbulk_1$ground_truth_proportions)
rowSums(cov_pbulk_1$ground_truth_proportions)[1:10]

# pseudo-bulk from the training split, and from the healthy-only split
train_pbulk   <- load_cov_pbulk("train")
healthy_pbulk <- load_cov_pbulk("healthy")

dim(train_pbulk$bulk_expression_profiles)
dim(healthy_pbulk$bulk_expression_profiles)
```

A typical benchmark workflow is therefore:

```{r covid-workflow, eval=FALSE}
train_cov <- load_cov_imm("train")
cov_pbulk_1 <- load_cov_pbulk(1)

bulk_expr <- cov_pbulk_1$bulk_expression_profiles
truth <- cov_pbulk_1$ground_truth_proportions

# res = run_deconvolution(bulk = bulk_expr,ref = train_cov)
# metrics = calculate_rsme_pearson(estimates= res,ground_ruth = truth)
```

### Reference-mismatch benchmarking

Swapping the matched reference for the healthy-only one gives a benchmark in which the reference no longer reflects the disease composition of the mixtures. Comparing the two runs on the same pseudo-bulk data isolates the effect of that mismatch on each method:

```{r covid-mismatch, eval=FALSE}
cov_pbulk_1 <- load_cov_pbulk(1)

matched  <- load_cov_imm("train")     # reference matching the mixtures
mismatch <- load_cov_imm("healthy")   # healthy-donor reference

# cell types the healthy reference cannot recover
setdiff(
  colnames(cov_pbulk_1$ground_truth_proportions),
  unique(as.character(mismatch$cell_type))
)

# res_matched  = run_deconvolution(bulk = cov_pbulk_1$bulk_expression_profiles, ref = matched)
# res_mismatch = run_deconvolution(bulk = cov_pbulk_1$bulk_expression_profiles, ref = mismatch)
```
